entities.name: Obstructive sleep apnea
observations: OSA severity was graded by apnea–hypopnea index (AHI): mild 5–14.9, moderate 15–29.9, and severe ≥30 events/hour; mean AHI was 21.9 ± 18.9 in the CAD cohort.

entities.name: Coronary artery disease
observations: The directly relevant prospective cohort included 190 patients with angiographically documented CAD who underwent overnight sleep testing.

entities.name: PMID:27502204
observations: Prospective cohort study in 190 CAD patients; LDL-C was measured every 3–6 months for 53.2 ± 25.3 months, with 8.1 ± 4.2 measurements per patient.

Greater OSA severity was associated with greater visit-to-visit LDL-C variability; AHI correlated with LDL-C VIM (r=0.183, p=0.016). Adjusted analysis found a 3.8% higher VIM per 10-unit AHI increase (95% CI 0.1%–7.4%; p=0.044).
The study supports association, not causation, and was identified as the only directly relevant study examining the exact OSA–LDL-C variability–CAD question.

entities.name: OSA LDL-C variability
observations: In CAD patients, higher AHI was independently associated with higher visit-to-visit LDL-C variability measured by variation independent of the mean (VIM).
